audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Leviathan speech: untamable sea-creature/chaos imagery, failed capture, terrifying presence, armor, flame/smoke poetry, weapon-resistance, and king over proud beasts. Preserved as mythic-poetic creature language.

verses.restored: Can you draw out Leviathan with a hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?

familiar.text: Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?

verses.restored: Can you put a rope in his nose, or pierce his jaw with a hook?

familiar.text: Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?

verses.restored: Will he make many pleas to you? Will he speak soft words to you?

familiar.text: Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee?

verses.restored: Will he cut a covenant with you, that you take him as servant forever?

familiar.text: Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever?

verses.restored: Will you play with him like a bird, or bind him for your young women?

familiar.text: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?

verses.restored: Will partners bargain over him? Will they divide him among merchants?

familiar.text: Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants?

verses.restored: Can you fill his skin with harpoons, or his head with fishing spears?

familiar.text: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears?

verses.restored: Lay your hand on him; remember the battle; you will not do it again.

familiar.text: Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.

verses.restored: Look, hope concerning him is false; is one not thrown down even at the sight of him?

familiar.text: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him?

verses.restored: No one is fierce enough to rouse him. Who then can stand before me?

familiar.text: None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?

verses.restored: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Whatever is under all the heavens is mine.

familiar.text: Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him? whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.

verses.restored: I will not keep silent about his limbs, his mighty strength, and his graceful frame.

familiar.text: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.

verses.restored: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who can enter his double bridle?

familiar.text: Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle?

verses.restored: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.

familiar.text: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about.

verses.restored: His back is rows of shields, shut up with a tight seal.

familiar.text: His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal.

verses.restored: One is so near another that no air can come between them.

familiar.text: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

verses.restored: They cling each to the other; they hold together and cannot be separated.

familiar.text: They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.

verses.restored: His sneezings flash light, and his eyes are like eyelids of dawn.

familiar.text: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

verses.restored: From his mouth go flaming torches; sparks of fire leap out.

familiar.text: Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out.

verses.restored: From his nostrils smoke goes out, like a boiling pot and reeds.

familiar.text: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.

verses.restored: His breath kindles coals, and flame goes out from his mouth.

familiar.text: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.

verses.restored: In his neck strength lodges, and before him dismay dances.

familiar.text: In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him.

verses.restored: The folds of his flesh cling together; they are firm upon him, not moved.

familiar.text: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved.

verses.restored: His heart is firm like stone, firm like the lower millstone.

familiar.text: His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone.

verses.restored: When he rises, mighty ones are afraid; because of crashing they miss themselves.

familiar.text: When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.

verses.restored: The sword that reaches him does not stand, nor spear, dart, or javelin.

familiar.text: The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon.

verses.restored: He counts iron as straw, bronze as rotten wood.

familiar.text: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.

verses.restored: The arrow does not make him flee; sling stones are turned to stubble for him.

familiar.text: The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble.

verses.restored: Clubs are counted as stubble; he laughs at the shaking of the javelin.

familiar.text: Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.

verses.restored: His undersides are sharp potsherds; he spreads a threshing sledge on the mud.

familiar.text: Sharp stones are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire.

verses.restored: He makes the deep boil like a pot; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.

familiar.text: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.

verses.restored: Behind him he leaves a shining wake; one would think the deep had white hair.

familiar.text: He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary.

verses.restored: On earth there is none like him, made without fear.

familiar.text: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.

verses.restored: He sees every high thing; he is king over all the sons of pride.

familiar.text: He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride.
